extracted.intended_audience: SoME4 participants, math content creators, and math educators / teachers
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and explanation of the supplementary SoME4 (Summer of Math Exposition) prizes for entries judged to be particularly helpful to teachers. Describes the selection process, the heuristics used, and examples of the kinds of content that won.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty, clarity, and memorability
rubrics_metrics.description: Past 'general' winners were chosen as entries the curator felt enthusiastic about recommending, as judged by novelty, clarity, and memorability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three axes were explicit criteria for prior general awards; they serve as high-level quality markers for content that stands out and is recommendable to a broad audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpful to teachers / teacher-usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: This year's supplementary prizes were intended to reward content that 'shows strong promise to be helpful to teachers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favored materials that teachers could actually use in their classrooms — not simply entertaining or clever pieces, but those that offer clear pedagogical value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher feedback-informed selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The organizers 'solicited teacher feedback on all the results and compiled them,' and used that feedback together with the curator's own review to choose winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teacher input was explicitly gathered and weighed; selection is not solely the curator's taste but informed by practicing educators' perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eagerness-to-share test (teacher empathy)
rubrics_metrics.description: As the curator reviewed each entry he asked, 'If I were teaching a course on this subject, how eager would I be to share with my students?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A useful heuristic: would a teacher be excited to incorporate the item into a course? This mental test guided whether something felt classroom-worthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modularity / pick-and-choose usability
rubrics_metrics.description: It was 'very rare' the curator would assign a video/article wholesale; instead he expected teachers to 'pick out bits and pieces, perhaps borrowing examples or pulling out interactive elements' for classroom use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials that are modular — easy to excerpt, adapt, or integrate into existing lessons — are preferred. Whole-course-length consumption is less important than usable fragments, examples, or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive elements and easily shareable demos
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for content that provides 'easily shareable set of demos' or interactive elements that can be dropped into lessons (example: Relativity in Desmos).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demos and interactive visualizations that teachers can directly share with students (links, embedded demos) increase an entry's classroom utility and were viewed favorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaffolding that enables student reinvention
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries that 'offer a nice scaffold that any probability teacher could use in a class ... to guide students to reinvent core concepts' were prized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that leads students step-by-step toward discovering or re-deriving an idea — rather than simply presenting the result — is especially valuable for teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite-level appropriateness / sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Some items are judged relative to where they fit in a curriculum (e.g., 'most relevant after having built up some of the fundamentals').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An entry's usefulness is judged partly by whether it matches the expected background of students and where it would slot into a course sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to sharpen student intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials that 'stand to sharpen a student's intuition' about a topic (e.g., spacetime diagrams for relativity) were considered valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that deepens conceptual understanding and intuition — not just technical facts — is more likely to be adopted by teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solving usefulness and practice opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Pieces that highlight 'a nice property of cubic functions useful for problem-solving' and offer acts of 'both using and proving it' give students practice with fundamental ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries that present techniques or tricks that are applicable in problem-solving and which also provide opportunities for proof or practice are desirable for classroom use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good framing and underlying motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: The curator appreciated 'the framing of the lesson here, and the underlying motivation' (example: Euclid's Algorithm presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong pedagogical framing and clear motivation for why a topic matters help teachers adopt material; presentation that situates a topic within broader context is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability as warmups / illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Some entries serve well as warmups or illustrative demonstrations (e.g., 'a nice warmup into any stat mech class'), and demos that can be 'pulled out by teachers to fit their specific lessons' were highlighted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that can function flexibly as an introductory activity, warmup, or illustrative example for a lesson is particularly useful for instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection subjectivity and non-exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The curator notes 'there is no perfect and objective way to do this' and urges readers to 'take the word "winner" with a heavy grain of salt' because many excellent contributions exist beyond the chosen five.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit guidance that selection is subjective; being a winner is not an absolute judgment of quality, and many non-winners may still be highly valuable to teachers.
